name: OPA2134UA_2K5
title: Low-distortion FET-input audio operational amplifiers: single, dual and quad
summary: The OPA134 (one amplifier), OPA2134 (two) and OPA4134 (four) are JFET-input operational amplifiers aimed at audio work, with 0.00008 % typical THD+N and 8 nV/√Hz input noise. They run from ±2.5 V to ±18 V (5 V to 36 V single), are stable at unity gain, give 8 MHz of gain-bandwidth and 20 V/µs of slew, and swing to about a volt from each rail. Each amplifier of the dual and quad has its own circuitry, and the output does not invert when the inputs leave the common-mode range.

circuits.title: 2nd-order, 30 kHz, multiple-feedback low-pass filter
circuits.description: One amplifier set up as an inverting multiple-feedback low-pass filter with a DC gain of –5 V/V (R4 / R1 = 2.94 kΩ / 590 Ω) and a 30 kHz corner, falling at 40 dB per decade. The input runs through R1 to a node that C2 returns to ground and R4 feeds back from the output; R3 carries that node to the inverting input, which C5 ties back to the output. The noninverting input is grounded. Targets: gain peaking under 3 dB.
notes: R1, R3, R4, C2 and C5 are the symbols of the transfer-function, gain and cutoff equations.
Supplies: ±2.5 V to ±18 V (5 V to 36 V single).

circuits.title: Distortion test circuit
circuits.description: A noninverting stage with R3 added between the two inputs. R3 leaves the signal gain at 1 + R2 / R1 but lowers the feedback, so the amplifier's own distortion appears 101 times larger, 1 + R2 / (R1 ∥ R3), and an audio analyzer can resolve it. The analyzer's generator drives the noninverting input; its input, loaded with 1 kΩ, reads the 3 Vrms output. R3 is kept small. Values: the signal-gain-11 set.

parts.note: amplifier A; measured on the OPA134

notes: Other sets: signal gain 1 with R1 absent and R3 = 10 Ω; signal gain 101 with R1 = 10 Ω and R3 absent; R2 = 1 kΩ in all.

operation.text: The input pair is p-channel JFETs, with cascode circuitry around it that keeps common-mode rejection high and bias current low over the whole input range. The amplifiers are stable at unity gain and stay well behaved with large load capacitance.
In the dual and quad every amplifier has separate circuitry, so one amplifier driven into overload or shorted at its output leaves the others working normally.

Across 20 Hz to 20 kHz into 2 kΩ, THD+N stays under 0.0004 %, and it stays fairly flat as the output swing grows. Headroom is counted against a 0.01 % THD+N limit, relative to 0.7746 Vrms (1 mW in 600 Ω); the maximum output under that limit is 11.7 Vrms, stated as 23.6 dBu.

Distortion is below what commercial analyzers resolve directly. Adding R3 across the inputs of a noninverting stage raises the noise gain to 101 while the signal gain, input signal and load stay the same, so the error the amplifier makes reads 101 times larger. The method is confirmed by repeating a measurement where distortion is large enough to read directly, at high gain or frequency.

The JFETs' input capacitance changes with common-mode voltage. In inverting use the inputs sit at virtual ground and this does not matter; in noninverting use, unequal impedances at the two inputs above 2 kΩ raise distortion. When the source impedance or R1 ∥ R2 exceeds 2 kΩ, put a matching resistance, RS = R1 ∥ R2, in series with the noninverting input. Low resistor values keep thermal noise down.
The output does not reverse phase when the inputs pass the common-mode range, even 10 V beyond it.
An internal limit holds output current near 36 mA sourcing and –30 mA sinking at 25 °C, and lower as the part warms.

Voltage noise dominates with low source impedance and current noise with high source impedance. The amplifier keeps both low, so it suits a wide span of sources, reactive ones included; above about 2 kΩ of source resistance it adds little to the resistor's own noise.

The amplifiers work from ±2.5 V to ±18 V (5 V to 36 V). Production test is at ±15 V; most behaviour holds across the full range, and the typical-characteristic curves show what moves with supply. More than 36 V across the supplies can damage the device.
Offset is laser-trimmed and normally needs no adjustment: under ±2 mV, with about 10 µV/°C typical drift over its operating temperature range.
Fit a 10 nF or larger low-ESR ceramic capacitor from each supply pin to ground, as near the pins as possible; on a single supply only V+ needs one.

Use a ground plane and keep analog and digital ground currents apart. Route input traces short and away from supply and output traces, crossing them at right angles where they must cross. Keeping the feedback and gain resistors tight against the inverting input cuts parasitic capacitance. Leakage into sensitive traces drops with a guard ring held at low impedance. Clean the board after assembly; after aqueous cleaning, bake it at 85 °C for 30 minutes to drive out moisture.
On the single, pins 1 and 5 are not to be connected and pin 8 has no internal connection.
